question: What main event causes urine to leak out in stress urinary incontinence?

options.D: Sudden physical pressure on the bladder

explanation: You've got this! Stress incontinence happens when sudden physical pressure—like coughing, laughing, or lifting—pushes urine out because the bladder pressure beats the urethra's grip. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h1)

question: Why do people often get confused by the word 'stress' in stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: They believe it is caused by mental exhaustion
options.B: They assume it only happens during high-intensity sports
options.C: They confuse it with neurological distress
options.D: They think it relates to emotional anxiety rather than physical pressure

explanation: It's an easy mix-up! In this case, 'stress' means physical force or pressure on your organs, not emotional stress or worry. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h1)

question: Which muscle group acts like a supportive hammock at the bottom of the pelvis?
explanation: Think of the levator ani as a strong sling or hammock holding all your pelvic organs neatly in place. Great job! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h2)

question: What is the main job of the urethral sphincter in normal bladder control?

options.A: To sense when the bladder is completely full
options.B: To push urine out of the bladder during voiding
options.C: To stay contracted and maintain a tight seal against urine leakage
options.D: To stretch when the bladder fills with urine

explanation: The urethral sphincter acts like a tight valve, staying closed to keep urine inside until you're ready to use the bathroom. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h2)

question: What happens to the bladder and urethra during 'urethral hypermobility' when a patient coughs?

options.A: The bladder instantly shrinks in size
options.B: The urethral sphincter locks tightly shut to block flow
options.C: The detrusor muscle contracts with too much force
options.D: The bladder and urethra drop downward due to weak support

explanation: When the pelvic tissues are a bit weak, coughing causes the bladder and urethra to sag downward instead of staying firmly in place. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h3)

question: What does 'intrinsic sphincter deficiency' mean?

options.A: Blockage of urine flow by the prostate gland
options.B: Damage or weakness of the urethral sphincter muscle itself
options.C: A temporary infection lining the urinary tract
options.D: Overactivity of the main bladder muscle

explanation: Simply put, the valve muscle itself has lost some of its strength and can no longer seal tightly on its own. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h3)

question: A patient with long-term severe bronchitis has a higher risk for which type of urine leakage?

options.A: Overflow incontinence due to a blocked prostate
options.B: Stress incontinence due to repeated pressure from coughing
options.C: Urge incontinence due to bladder muscle irritation

explanation: Constant coughing creates repeated downward pressure on the pelvic floor, which can wear down its support over time. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a common risk factor for stress urinary incontinence?

options.C: Frequent high-fluid intake throughout the day

explanation: Drinking plenty of water is healthy! The real risk factors involve things that weaken pelvic support, like childbirth, hormonal shifts, or heavy pressure. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h4)

question: Why is a urinalysis always done when checking for stress incontinence?

options.A: To check kidney function and filtration rates
options.B: To measure the exact amount of residual urine left in the bladder
options.C: To test the patient for diabetes and high blood sugar levels
options.D: To rule out a urinary tract infection that can cause similar symptoms

explanation: Infections can mimic incontinence by irritating the bladder, so checking the urine first helps doctors make a clear diagnosis. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h5)

question: What is the purpose of a cough stress test during a physical checkup?

options.A: To check if coughing triggers a bladder spasm
options.B: To test the strength of the patient's respiratory muscles
options.C: To measure lung capacity while the patient lies flat
options.D: To observe if physical pressure causes immediate urine leakage

explanation: By asking the patient to cough, the clinician can watch directly to see if pressure causes any accidental leakage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h5)

question: A nurse is teaching a patient how to do Kegel exercises correctly. What is the key instruction?

options.A: Contract the pelvic floor muscles as if trying to stop the flow of urine
options.B: Squeeze the abdominal and thigh muscles tightly while holding your breath
options.C: Push down gently as if having a bowel movement
options.D: Flex the buttocks and hips until your pelvis rises off the bed

explanation: Spot on! Kegels are all about squeezing those pelvic floor muscles—just like you're pausing your urine stream mid-flow, without squeezing your tummy or thighs. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h6)

question: Which lifestyle change helps the most in managing stress incontinence?

options.A: Drinking less than two cups of fluid per day
options.B: Achieving and maintaining a healthy body weight
options.C: Eliminating all forms of physical exercise completely
options.D: Increasing daily intake of carbonated beverages

explanation: Shedding extra pounds takes a huge amount of constant pressure off the pelvic floor muscles. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h6)

question: What is the main surgical option used to treat severe stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: Widening the urethral opening with a stent
options.B: Placing a supportive sling under the urethra
options.C: Implanting an artificial kidney to filter urine
options.D: Removing the lower portion of the bladder

explanation: A surgical sling acts like a little hammock or seatbelt underneath the urethra to keep it from dropping when you move. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h7)

question: Why are pills and medications rarely the main treatment for stress incontinence?

options.A: Surgical options and pelvic therapy target the mechanical cause much more effectively
options.B: Medications for stress incontinence always cause permanent kidney damage
options.C: Pills are unable to dissolve inside the human digestive tract
options.D: Doctors prefer lifestyle changes because drugs are illegal for this use

explanation: Since stress incontinence is a physical, mechanical problem of loose support, fixing it requires physical strengthening or surgery rather than drugs. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h7)

question: What is a very common emotional or social challenge for patients with chronic stress incontinence?

options.A: False belief that they are pregnant
options.C: Severe memory loss and cognitive decline
options.D: Social isolation and anxiety about public leaks

explanation: The fear of leaking in public can make patients feel embarrassed, causing them to stay home and miss out on social life. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h8)

question: Which skin problem happens most often when urinary incontinence is left untreated?

options.A: Deep pressure ulcers over the shoulder blades
options.B: Dry, scaly skin patches across the upper arms
options.C: Perineal dermatitis and breakdown from moisture
options.D: Fungal rashes spreading across the face and chest

explanation: When skin stays in contact with urine too long, the moisture breaks down the skin barrier and causes painful irritation or rashes. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h8)
